claim_being_audited: The actor recommends `certify_model` on the theory that aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout starts at 6% with rollback and monitoring, and certification is still supportable if the supply-chain vendor screening limitation is expressly disclosed because the exposed segment remains below target and the current risk acceptance draft is unsigned and incomplete.
decision_criteria: If admissible evidence shows the model card already discloses the material limitation for the exposed named use case before launch, the verdict could improve.
If admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance that expressly covers the exposed supply-chain vendor screening segment before launch, the verdict could improve.
If the rollout plan is changed to exclude the affected use case until the weakness is resolved, the certification rationale would be materially stronger.
Without one of those predicates, aggregate readiness and deployment monitoring are insufficient under the stated policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the final approved model card or release packet showing explicit disclosure of the supply-chain vendor screening sanctions-risk explanation limitation for the named launch use case.
Provide an approved risk acceptance, if any, signed by the proper approver and expressly addressing continued exposure of the supply-chain vendor screening segment.
Provide the final launch-go/no-go record showing whether certification was conditioned on that disclosure being completed before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected supply-chain vendor screening use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The segment is below target on sanctions-risk explanation, which is the material weakness at issue.
The available risk acceptance draft is not approved because the approver line is blank.
The draft also does not address the exposed supply-chain vendor screening segment.
The governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring do not cure the weakness when the affected segment remains exposed.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure for the named use case has actually been completed before launch.
unsupported_claims: The current record does not support certifying the model now, because a required predicate for launch compliance remains unproven.
The current record does not support treating 6% rollout, rollback, or monitoring as a substitute for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that certification is presently policy-compliant is unsupported absent evidence of an actual model-card disclosure covering the named exposed use case.
